Definition: to be rabid (figuratively, insane); also (from the exhaustion of frenzy) to languish
BiblicalUsage: To faint or to be mad is the word for a mind unstrung, and its two appearances are a famine and a madman. In Genesis 47:13 the land of Egypt and Canaan "fainted by reason of the famine," and in Proverbs 26:18 the madman "casteth firebrands, arrows, and death."
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that the word's two pictures belong together: famine faints a whole land, and madness throws firebrands at its neighbours, and both are what happens when life comes apart.
